title: Exhaustion terminal is pinned only at the SQL layer — neither live call site (delivery webhooks, wrong-person route) is handler-tested
detail: Round-specific traceability #4 (exhaustion LIVE) is only half covered. `second_failure_exhausts_to_unreachable_with_signal_test` drives `rc_sql.exhaust_reference_call` + `rc_sql.stamp_referee_contact_invalid` directly (SQL authority: queued/contact_initiated guard, status→unreachable, next_attempt_at NULL, result set, stamp asserted in fraud_signals) and `exhaustion_guard_only_fires_from_live_states_test` pins the sticky-terminal 0-row stand-down. But the two production branches that route a corrected row into exhaustion — `correction_cycles >= 1 → exhaust_row` in `webhooks.gleam` (resend/twilio handlers, lines ~287/437) and the same gate in `form_handler.apply_wrong_person`/`exhaust_wrong_person` (lines ~1218/1262) — have NO test: no test seeds a row with correction_cycles=1 and fires a signed bounce / SMS failure / wrong-person POST through the actual handler. The orchestration those branches own — `reference_call_correction_exhausted` audit row, `notify_reference_correction_exhausted` in-app notification, stamp-after-transition sequencing, and the 0-row → redirect stand-down — is entirely untested (grep confirms `correction_cycles` appears in no other test file; `reference_checks_webhooks_integration_test.gleam` and `reference_exit_routes_integration_test.gleam` were not updated by this PR and cover only the first-failure → awaiting_correction branch). A miswire of the branch gate (e.g., inverted comparison, wrong event type) would pass every green test and break the second-failure flow in production. First-failure-does-NOT-exhaust is only implicitly pinned (webhook tests assert awaiting_correction after a bounce on a fresh row); no test asserts fraud_signals is untouched on first failure.
recommended_fix: Extend `reference_checks_webhooks_integration_test.gleam` with a test that seeds a row with correction_cycles=1 (queued) and posts a svix-signed bounce asserting: status=unreachable, referee_contact_invalid stamped, `reference_call_correction_exhausted` audit count 1, one in-app notification; mirror it for the twilio handler and for `handle_wrong_person_post` (wrong-person on a corrected row → exhaust, not awaiting_correction); add a boundary assertion that a first failure on a cycles=0 row leaves fraud_signals unstamped.

title: Substitute single-submit test can pass vacuously — row-shape assertions skip silently on the exact regression it targets
detail: In `substitute_creates_new_row_and_audits_old_and_new_ids_test` (reference_checks_actions_integration_test.gleam ~line 600), the core assertions (old row retained with status objected, exactly one successor with new trio queued + cadence armed, new id != old id) live inside `case returned.rows { [old_row, new_row] -> ... ; _ -> Nil }` with an inner `_, _ -> Nil` fallthrough — if the query returns 0, 1, or 3+ rows (e.g., a duplicate-successor insert regression), every row-level assertion is skipped and the test still passes. The audit check is also soft: `has_both_ids` can evaluate True with `new_id = ""` because `"new_reference_call_id": "` is a substring of any details JSON carrying the key. Mitigation: `substitute_is_idempotent_and_guarded_test` hard-asserts a slot-scoped count of exactly 2 on the double-submit path (which would catch a duplicate insert), and the `app_trio` fallthrough `_ -> Nil` similarly softens the app-trio assertion. The suite being green does not prove the single-submit shape assertions ever execute.
recommended_fix: Replace the `case ... _ -> Nil` fallthroughs with `should.fail()` arms (or `let assert` on the decoded shapes) so a shape mismatch fails the test instead of silently passing; derive `new_id` with a `should.fail()`-style extraction rather than a `""` default.

title: RC4.3 payload additions (contact snapshot, corrected trio, taken_over_at, correction_cycles) have no positive wire assertion in server tests
detail: `sample_reference_call_row` in application_detail_handler_test.gleam now carries taken_over_at, contact_name/email/phone, corrected_*, correction_cycles, and `encode_reference_call` serializes them (verified in application_detail_handler.gleam:1193-1215), but none of the encode tests assert any of the new keys appear on the wire — they only re-check the RC4.1/RC4.2 keys and the internal-marker guard. `reference_detail_payload_integration_test.gleam` swapped its negative control from `larry@example.com` to `form_token_internal_sentinel` (sound: form_token is still asserted absent in `detail_payload_strips_internal_fields_test`, and the positive controls `reference_call_id`/`attempt_count` remain), but it also lacks a positive assertion that contact data now rides the payload — the very contract the §7.7 take-over chips and §8.3 edit prefill depend on. A regression dropping contact_name/contact_email/corrected_* from the encoder would pass every server test and break the client UI.
recommended_fix: Add assertions to `encode_reference_call_strips_internal_fields_test` (or a new unit test) that the wire contains contact_name, contact_email, corrected_name:null, taken_over_at, and correction_cycles, and add a positive `string.contains(body, "\"contact_email\"")` check to the detail-payload integration test.

title: Advisory test gate: CONCERNS
detail: All four claimed counts verified by actual execution at ace27b1 on a freshly migrated test DB: 512/512 integration, 1476 server unit, 540 client, 110 shared — all green. P0 state-machine guards are pinned: take-over pre-state guard + taken_over_at + cadence clear + sweep exclusion (dedicated test) + late-completion transition + audit; correct one-cycle (second correct 409s, snapshot immutable, correction_cycles=1, re-arm, audit); substitute idempotency (exactly 2 rows + 1 audit on double-submit, refused 409); exhaustion SQL transition + referee_contact_invalid stamp + terminal stand-down; ownership/authz negative (cross-landlord 404, no audit); 400 trio validation. P1 gaps: the two exhaustion call-site branches (webhooks + wrong-person route) are covered only at the SQL layer, not through the handlers — ~2 of 13 round-specific traceability items only partially pinned (≈85-90% P1). Gate: CONCERNS.
recommended_fix: Add the handler-level exhaustion tests described in the first finding (signed bounce / SMS failure / wrong-person POST against a correction_cycles=1 row asserting unreachable + stamp + audit + notification, plus a first-failure no-stamp boundary). That closes the last P1 gap and raises the gate to PASS; the soft-assertion cleanup in the substitute test would harden it further.
